rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a nickel coating on W particles followed by spark-plasma sintering, whereas the hidden target uses liquid-metal dealloying of a WTaVTi RHEA precursor in molten Cu to create a bicontinuous composite. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies spark-plasma sintering conditions, while the hidden target uses vacuum-sealed immersion in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h. The service conditions (fusion-reactor heat transfer joints under irradiation) are mentioned in both, but the processing regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a reactive Ni coating forming an interfacial alloy to improve wetting and suppress voids. The hidden target's mechanism relies on selective dissolution of Ti from interdendritic channels into Cu, leaving W-rich passivating interlayers and aligned Cu channels. These are different classes of mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced voids, lower thermal interface resistance, and improved mechanical integrity relative to vapor-coated W powders. The hidden target predicts and measures substantially increased thermal conductivity surpassing pure W at high temperature and reduced He-induced swelling relative to pure W. The predicted properties and directions are different.
